prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere products, predictable latency, documented quality). External: spacecraft, launch segment, user processing environments. Elements: Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time authority, pass supervision, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule, receives station constraint notices, hosts primary routing policy point; contacts have readiness check, live monitoring, post-pass closure. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): orbit, maneuvers; sends visibility predictions, antenna pointing products to planning. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): processing, calibration, distribution staging; downlink allocation with Primary (nominal) and Backup (failover, routinely tested) Processing Clusters. Network Control System (Lantern): WAN status, path selection, maintenance windows, station allocations, antenna readiness, contact start/end; sends MCC antenna status, link config, timing references, routing readiness pre-pass; vets timing alarms for Spacecraft Operations Team. Long Term Archive: Primary Cluster-to-LTA transfers rate limited during contacts. User Services Portal. Mission Planning System: receives contact booking requests. Command Validation Gateway: pre-uplink check. Telemetry Ingest Service: receives real-time frames, validates framing/time continuity, records reception metadata; produces Pass Replay Packet post-contact for engineering review. Orbit Determination Engine: state updates, Doppler Residual Report per pass, basis for visibility/maneuver/pointing predictions. Product Quality Service. Ground Network Manager (Juniper): antenna assignment, link availability, site coordination, conflict arbitration, Antenna Deicing Notice, pins critical paths pre-AOS, latency breach diagnosis, consults Cybersecurity Desk before blocking. Antennas: North/South S-Band (command, low-rate telemetry; North nominal uplink) via protected routers to MCC; Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band (high-rate downlink), dual WAN to PPF. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team (monitors health at MCC consoles; roles: console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands via CVG, pauses on mismatch; telemetry engineer checks quality/loss/latency; spacecraft systems engineer checks flight rules, records anomalies), Flight Dynamics Team (tracking/time tags for orbit assessment), Payload Calibration Team, Cybersecurity Desk (Security Exception Ticket), station operators. Pass reconstruction after close: command history, telemetry timing, station status, logs into narrative; confirms objectives. Rules: daily cut-off freeze; contingency needs justification; safety>timeliness>efficiency; X-band moved on precipitation; routing: approved

New part:
S093: The Mission Control Center coordinates with the Payload Processing Facility when instrument mode changes, data downlink priorities, or reception gaps could affect downstream processing.
S094: The Payload Calibration Team sends the Calibration Patch Bundle after calibration analysis identifies an approved update for payload processing behavior.
S095: Subsystem specialists are not expected to staff every live contact, but they must be reachable during planned critical activities and whenever a console operator declares an off-nominal condition.
S096: Escalation from the Mission Control Center begins with the console lead, moves to the responsible discipline lead, and then reaches mission management when the condition threatens spacecraft safety, contact continuity, or recovery schedule.
S097: The Spacecraft Operations Team and Flight Dynamics Team coordinate closely before orbit-control activities so that command timing, attitude constraints, tracking expectations, and post-burn assessment steps remain consistent.
S098: When telemetry indicates a possible onboard fault, operators preserve the command state, avoid discretionary commanding, and request specialist review before changing spacecraft configuration.
S099: The Mission Planning System receives operational constraints from mission control after anomalies, station outages, or spacecraft configuration changes require adjustment of future contacts or payload activities.
S100: At the end of each shift, the Mission Control Center records unresolved actions, open engineering questions, and expected specialist responses so that the next operations crew can maintain continuity without relying on informal handover.
S101: Mission planning begins when observation requests arrive through the User Services Portal or from internal operations channels at the Mission Control Center.
S102: The Mission Planning System, also called Cedar in this section, is the authoritative tool for assembling candidate observation timelines and associated ground contact activities.
S103: Each request is checked for requester authority, target definition, time sensitivity, acquisition mode, expected data volume, and any handling restrictions before it is admitted to the planning pool.
S104: The User Services Portal records the request state so that external users can distinguish accepted requests from those still awaiting technical review.
S105: The Spacecraft Operations Team reviews late operational requests when they affect spacecraft attitude, thermal margin, stored command capacity, or contact preparation.
S106: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit predictions and visibility assumptions that the planning cycle uses to determine feasible imaging windows and ground contacts.
S107: The Mission Planning System combines request priority, instrument availability, contact opportunities, onboard storage margin, and downlink capacity into a draft activity schedule.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
